title: Efficient Code Generation for Data-Intensive Simulink Models via Redundancy Elimination
problem: Simulink code generators employ optimization techniques like expression folding and variable reuse, but fail to detect and eliminate redundant calculations present in data-intensive models. This oversight significantly degrades efficiency and performance of generated embedded code.
motivation: Simulink is critical infrastructure for embedded software development, and eliminating redundancy in generated code directly improves performance for data-intensive embedded applications.
method: The approach scans Simulink block diagrams to identify calculations that are performed multiple times, then removes those redundancies while generating the code. It builds on existing optimizations (expression folding to simplify expressions, and variable reuse to avoid recalculation) by adding detection specifically for repeated-computation patterns in data-intensive embedded workloads.
key_novelty: Simulink's code generator uses a dedicated redundancy-detection step to eliminate repeated calculations in data-intensive embedded models.
contributions: Identification and characterization of redundancy patterns in data-intensive Simulink models
Redundancy elimination optimization technique for code generation
Improved code efficiency for embedded data processing applications
